title: Quasar radiation transforms the gas in a merging companion galaxy
question: Investigate the galactic environment of quasar J 012555.11−012925.00 at z ≈ 2.7 and directly assess the impact of quasar radiation on the physical state and small-scale structure of molecular gas in its merging companion galaxy.

data.sensitivity: Band 3 continuum rms: 8.3 uJy/beam; Band 6 continuum rms: 14.8 uJy/beam (multiband), ~25 uJy/beam (individual SPWs); Line cube spectral rms: 0.29 - 0.37 mJy/beam

what.value: X-shooter composite quasar spectrum used to model dust reddening and unabsorbed continuum.

evidence.quote: The spectrum of J 012555.11 012925.00 appears clearly reddened compared to the X-shooter composite quasar spectrum, [62] as shown in Extended Data Fig. 5.

what.value: CO excitation line ratios r_31 = 0.8 and r_71 = 0.2 for molecular gas mass conversion.

evidence.quote: Assuming [53] 𝑟31 = 0.8 and 𝑟71 = 0.2 we obtain 𝑀H2 = (1.0 ± 0.1) × 10^10 𝑀⊙ (companion) and 𝑀H2 = (5.5 ± 0.1) × 10^9 𝑀⊙ (host),

recipe.goal: Search ALMA cubes for millimeter line emission, create moment maps, and measure continuum fluxes
recipe.method: Blindly searched ALMA cubes for line emission using SOFIA v2.0 with residual continuum subtraction and the smooth+clip (S+C) algorithm; created moment 0, 1, and 2 maps; smoothed CO(7-6) to CO(3-2) resolution for line ratio map; measured continuum flux densities in Band 3 and Band 6 images.
key_parameters: Detection threshold = 3.5 sigma; moment 1 and 2 pixel threshold = 1.5 times local rms; non-detection 3 sigma upper limits assume line FWHM = 100 km/s.
assumptions: Line FWHM of 100 km s^-1 for 3 sigma upper limits of non-detections.

recipe.goal: Decompose optical broad-band images and extract 1D spectra of the quasar, companion galaxy, and quasar host galaxy
recipe.method: Fitted Subaru HSC g and r band images with Galfit using a PSF + sky + two Sersic (n=1.0) components; extracted 1D quasar spectrum and disentangled companion galaxy spectrum from 2D X-shooter PA=90 deg spectra by fitting two Moffat profiles across rebinned wavelength bins; extracted quasar host galaxy residual emission from dark troughs of saturated absorption lines.
key_parameters: Sersic index = 1.0; X-shooter rebinning: 200 pixels (40 A) for UVB/VIS, 800 pixels (480 A) for NIR; slit widths: 1.0, 0.9, 1.2 arcsec for UVB, VIS, NIR.
assumptions: Companion galaxy spatial profile width is the quadratic sum of the unresolved quasar seeing and the 0.9'' width derived from Galfit, located 0.55'' from the quasar.

recipe.goal: Spectrophotometric SED modelling of the companion and quasar host galaxies
recipe.method: Fitted Subaru HSC photometry, ALMA mm-continuum constraints, and X-shooter SEDs for both companion and host galaxies using the bagpipes code.
key_parameters: Stellar birth cloud lifetime = 10 Myr; velocity dispersion = 500 km s^-1; free U_min and gamma for dust emission.
assumptions: Double power law star formation history (SFH) model and standard Calzetti dust extinction law; standard LambdaCDM cosmology (H0 = 70 km s^-1 Mpc^-1, Omega_Lambda = 0.7, Omega_m = 0.3).

recipe.goal: Estimate molecular gas, dust, and SMBH masses
recipe.method: Converted CO(7-6) and CO(3-2) line luminosities L'_CO into M_H2; estimated dust masses from ALMA Band 6 continuum assuming a gray body spectrum; estimated SMBH mass from C IV and H-beta emission line FWHMs and reddening-corrected continuum luminosities at 1350 A and 5100 A.
key_parameters: r_31 = 0.8, r_71 = 0.2, alpha_CO = 0.8 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1; dust beta = 0.7, T_dust = 20 to 60 K.
assumptions: CO excitation ratios r_31 = 0.8, r_71 = 0.2; CO-to-H2 conversion factor alpha = 0.8 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1; gray body dust spectrum with beta = 0.7 and T = 20-60 K; standard single-epoch virial SMBH scaling relations.

recipe.goal: Analyse differential dust extinction and fit multi-component Voigt profiles to HI, H2, metal, CI, and CO absorption lines
recipe.method: Compared quasar spectrum to X-shooter composite reddened with an SMC-like extinction curve (quasar pair method); fitted multi-component Voigt profiles to HI, H2 (2 components), low-ionization metals (18 components), CI fine-structure levels (6 components), and CO A-X bands (2 components) using the spectro package with a partial coverage factor C_f.
key_parameters: 11th order Chebyshev polynomial adjustment for HI continuum; 2 components for H2; 18 components for metals (Gaussian prior on b: mean 6 km/s, sigma 2 km/s); 6 components for CI (T_CMB = 10 K at z = 2.662); 2 components for CO (b = 3 +/- 1 km/s, log T [K] = 2 +/- 0.3).
assumptions: SMC-like extinction curve; single partial coverage factor C_f across components and wavelengths; tied Doppler b for J=0,1 H2 levels; turbulence-dominated broadening for low-ionization metals; one-zone radiative + collisional excitation + CMB (10 K) for CI fine-structure levels; Boltzmann rotational distribution for CO.

recipe.goal: Model physical conditions (number density and distance to the quasar) of the absorbing molecular gas
recipe.method: Modelled H2 ro-vibrational level column densities and CO column density using a 2D grid of constant-density PDR models computed with the Meudon PDR code (v1.5.4) in the number density-distance (n-d) plane, and cross-checked with CI fine-structure excitation and analytical HI/H2 transition theory.
key_parameters: Metallicity = 0.1 Solar; cosmic ray ionization rate = 10^-16 s^-1 per H2; LMC extinction curve with R_V = 2.6; MRN dust size distribution; dust-to-gas mass ratio = 0.01; turbulent velocity = 2 km s^-1.
assumptions: Constant-density slab illuminated on one side by scaled Mathis UV field mimicking the quasar radiation at distance d.

answer_key.quantity: Adopted Band 6 (226 GHz) continuum flux density (companion)

evidence.quote: Based on measurements in SPWs 21, 23 and 25 of band 6, we adopt continuum flux densities at ≈ 226 GHz to be 330±30 𝜇Jy and < 180 uJy for companion and host galaxies, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Adopted Band 6 (226 GHz) continuum flux density (quasar host)

evidence.quote: Based on measurements in SPWs 21, 23 and 25 of band 6, we adopt continuum flux densities at ≈ 226 GHz to be 330±30 𝜇Jy and < 180 uJy for companion and host galaxies, respectively.

answer_key.quantity: Band 3 (101.9 GHz) continuum flux density upper limit (both galaxies)

evidence.quote: We adopt a 3𝜎 upper limit of 25 𝜇Jy for the quasar and the companion galaxy.

evidence.quote: We obtained log 𝑁(HI) = 21.911+0.016−0.014 at 𝑧 = 2.66347+0.00024−0.00027 and a zero-level flux level 7.8+0.5−0.2 ×10^19 erg cm−2 s−1 Å−1,

answer_key.quantity: Total H2 column density towards quasar (log N(H2))

evidence.quote: We found the the total column density is log 𝑁(H2) = 21.19+0.02−0.01.
The levels 𝐽 = 0 and 1 provide estimates of the kinetic temperatures 𝑇𝑘 ≈ 𝑇01 = 320+40−20 K and 300+20−20 K for components 𝐴 and 𝐵, respectively.
The levels 𝐽 = 0 and 1 provide estimates of the kinetic temperatures 𝑇𝑘 ≈ 𝑇01 = 320+40−20 K and 300+20−20 K for components 𝐴 and 𝐵, respectively.

We obtain the average metallicity from the ratio of the total column density of the volatile element zinc to that of the total hydrogen column density 𝑁tot(H) = N(H i) + 2N(H2), giving log 𝑍/𝑍⊙ = −0.92 ± 0.03 (respective to Solar [76]).
In addition, the presence and the excitation of H2 constrains the gas density to be 𝑛H ∼ 10^5 − 10^6 cm−3.
The high density and measured column density imply that the molecular clouds are very compact, with sizes, 𝐿 ≈ 𝑁/𝑛H (assuming constant density) of less than 0.02 pc.

score_reason: All raw datasets (ALMA, VLT/X-shooter, Subaru HSC) and key analysis codes (SOFIA, bagpipes, Galfit, spectro, Meudon PDR, emcee) are publicly available and clearly identified, with priors and physical assumptions well documented; minor deductions for manual B-spline continuum placement and reliance on external Supplementary Tables for component-level parameters.
